'''Anamaría Font Villarroel''' is a Venezuelan [[theoretical physicist]] and professor of the [[Central University of Venezuela]] (UCV). Her research has been focused on models about the primordial components of matter in the context of [[string theory]].

Font has contributed to development of [[Calabi–Yau manifold|Calabi–Yau]] dimensional [[Compactification (physics)|compactification]] and she and her collaborators introduced the concept of [[S-duality]] to [[superstring theory]], contributing to the [[History of string theory|second superstring revolution]].

== Early life and education ==
Anamaría Font Villarroel was born in [[Anaco, Venezuela]]. In school she was supported by her teacher for her love of chemistry and physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Anamaria Font For Women In Science 2023 Laureate |website=L'Oréal |date=29 May 2020 |url=https://www.loreal.com/en/articles/commitments/professor-anamaria-font/ |access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref> She obtained her bachelor's degree in [[physics]], Cum Laude in 1980 from [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simon Bolivar University]], in Caracas, Venezuela.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://revistapersea.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Mujeres-en-Ciencias-final.pdf|title=López, L., & Ranaudo, M. A. (2016). Mujeres en Ciencia: Venezuela}}</ref>  

== Academic career ==
Font received a PhD from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1987, under the supervision of Austin M. Gleeson. Her PhD thesis was titled ''Four-Dimensional Supergravity Theories Arising from Superstrings''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last1=Font Villarroel |first1=A |title=Four-dimensional supergravity theories arising from superstrings |date=1987 |oclc=4434458540 |osti=5741159 |bibcode=1987PhDT........43F }}</ref> While pursuing her PhD,  she received classes from Nobel Prize physicist [[Steven Weinberg]].<ref name=":0" /> After completing her PhD she moved to France to work as a postdoctoral fellow in the [[Laboratoire d'Annecy-le-Vieux de physique des particules|Annecy-le-Vieux Particle Physics Laboratory]] (LAPP).<ref name=":0" /> Since 1989, she has been a physics professor at the [[Universidad Central de Venezuela]] in Caracas, Venezuela.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://fisica.ciens.ucv.ve/~afont/afont.html|title=Anamaria Font|website=fisica.ciens.ucv.ve}}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=February 2020}} She was also a visiting professor at the Arnold Sommerfeld Center<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theorie.physik.uni-muenchen.de/|title=Arnold Sommerfeld Center - LMU Munich|website=www.theorie.physik.uni-muenchen.de}}</ref> for theoretical physics in Munich, Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Faculty of Physics LMU ASC|url=https://www.theorie.physik.uni-muenchen.de/lsluest/members/former_mem/former_asc/anamaria_font/index.html|access-date=14 March 2021}}</ref>

Her 1990 article with Luis E. Ibañez, [[Dieter Lüst]] and [[Fernando Quevedo]] titled "Strong-weak coupling duality and non-perturbative effects in string theory"<ref name="cds.cern.ch">{{cite journal |last1=Font |first1=A. |last2=Ibáñez |first2=L.E. |last3=Lüst |first3=D. |last4=Quevedo |first4=F. |title=Strong-weak coupling duality and non-perturbative effects in string theory |journal=Physics Letters B |date=October 1990 |volume=249 |issue=1 |pages=35–43 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(90)90523-9 |bibcode=1990PhLB..249...35F |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/209981 }}</ref> had a big influence in the [[History of string theory|second superstring revolution]] in 1995. It was in this article where the term [[S-duality]] was first used in this context.<ref>{{cite book |last=Szabo |first=Richard J |title=An Introduction to String Theory and D-Brane Dynamics |year=2004 |isbn=978-1-86094-427-7 |pages=1–8 |chapter=A Brief History of String Theory |doi=10.1142/9781848162150_0001}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schwarz |first=John H. |date=1997-05-01 |title=Lectures on superstring and M theory dualities |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0920563297000704 |journal=Nuclear Physics B - Proceedings Supplements |volume=55 |issue=2 |pages=1–32 |doi=10.1016/S0920-5632(97)00070-4 |issn=0920-5632|arxiv=hep-th/9607201 |bibcode=1997NuPhS..55....1S }}</ref><ref name=":0" />

In 2013, Font was elected a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS) for the advancement of science in developing countries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Font, Anamaría |url=https://twas.org/directory/font-anamaria |website=TWAS}}</ref>

Font has been actively involved in projects related to education in physics and mathematics in Venezuela and other countries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Organizing committee |url=https://fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar/particulas/lass07/comite_org.html |website=fisica.cab.cnea.gov.ar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=6th ICTP Latin-American String School (Mexico City) |url=https://www.ictp-saifr.org/6th-ictp-latin-american-string-school-mexico-city/ |website=www.ictp-saifr.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=4th Joint Dutch-Brazil School on Theoretical Physics |url=https://www.ictp-saifr.org/4th-joint-dutch-brazil-school-on-theoretical-physics/ |website=www.ictp-saifr.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 Colombia |url=http://archive.schools.cimpa.info/anciensite/Anglais/AnciensProg/2003/Colombia03.html |website=archive.schools.cimpa.info}}</ref> In July 2018, ''[[Physics Today]]'' magazine published an interview with Font about the status of science in Venezuela.<ref>{{Cite journal |last= Feder |first= Tori |date=July 10, 2018 |title=Q&A: Anamaría Font on the deterioration of science in Venezuela |journal=Physics Today |issue= 7 |article-number= 31025 |doi=10.1063/PT.6.4.20180710a |bibcode= 2018PhT..2018g1025F |s2cid=240367242}}</ref> The publication data base [[INSPIRE-HEP]] included three of her notorious publications into their data base.<ref>{{Cite web |title=INSPIRE HEP |url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1009735 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419043523/https://inspirehep.net/authors/1009735 |archive-date=19 April 2021}}</ref>

She is a member of the [[Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World]] (OWSD).<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2015 |title=Font, Anamaria |url=https://owsd.net/member/font-anamaria-6 |website=owsd.net}}</ref>

Font is also a Severo Ochoa IFT (Instituto de Física Teórica) research associate.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anamaría Font, SO(IFT) Research Associate, has beeen [sic] awarded in the 25th annual L'Oréal-UNESCO International Prize 'Women and Science' {{!}} Instituto de Física Teórica |url=https://www.ift.uam-csic.es/en/news/anamar%C3%ADa-font-soift-research-associate-has-beeen-awarded-25th-annual-lor%C3%A9al-unesco |access-date=2023-06-20 |website=www.ift.uam-csic.es}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

Anamaria has 2 younger sisters, and a two half-siblings.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://utphysicshistory.net/AnamariaFont.html|title=UTPhysicsHistorySite|website=utphysicshistory.net}}</ref>  In December 2017, Anamaria married Stefan Theisan, a physicist,  after being together since 2001.<ref name="auto"/>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1991, Font was awarded the [[Lorenzo Mendoza Fleury Science Prize]]. Given by the country's national private industry, the prize recognizes the work of Venezuelan scientists, and is the most important scientific prize in Venezuela.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fundacionempresaspolar.org/|title=Fundación Empresas Polar|website=www.fundacionempresaspolar.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-14|title=Premio Fundacion Empresas Polar "Lorenzo Mendoza Feury"|url=https://bibliofep.fundacionempresaspolar.org/publicaciones/periodicas/ediciones-del-premio-lorenzo-mendoza-fleury/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190201133728/http://bibliofep.fundacionempresaspolar.org:80/publicaciones/periodicas/ediciones-del-premio-lorenzo-mendoza-fleury |archive-date=1 February 2019 }}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=February 2020}}

In 1998, she was awarded, jointly with [[Fernando Quevedo]], the [[ICTP Prize]] in the field of [[High energy physics|High Energy Physics]] (in honour of [[Yang Chen-Ning|Chen Ning Yang]]),<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=International Center for Theoretical Physics |title=ICTP Prize winners 1998 |url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-ictp-prize/the-prize-winners/ictp-prize-winners-1998.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704091619/https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-ictp-prize/the-prize-winners/ictp-prize-winners-1998.aspx |archive-date=4 July 2018 |access-date=14 March 2021 |website=ICTP}}</ref>

{{quote| "for their contribution to the phenomenological studies in superstring theory based on orbifold compactifications and many works on [[Calabi–Yau manifold|Calabi–Yau]] compactifications, [[mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]] and duality symmetries. These works have contributed to a greater understanding of the low energy string physics, as well as various stringy symmetries. In particular, the important concept of [[S-duality]] has been introduced by them and their collaborators."<ref name="cds.cern.ch"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Candelas |first1=Philip |last2=de la Ossa |first2=Xenia |last3=Font |first3=Anamaría |last4=Katz |first4=Sheldon |author-link4=Sheldon Katz |last5=Morrison |first5=David R. |title=Mirror symmetry for two-parameter models (I) |journal=Nuclear Physics B |date=March 1994 |volume=416 |issue=2 |pages=481–538 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(94)90322-0 |arxiv=hep-th/9308083 |bibcode=1994NuPhB.416..481C |s2cid=18490701 }}</ref>{{clarify |date=February 2020 |reason=This is floating without suitable context. This needs some type of in-text attribution. I cannot access the source to find out that context, but it could be introduced with something maybe like "The ICTP committee stated at the award ceremony that the prize was given:}} }}

In 2023, Font was awarded the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards]], representing Latin America'',''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Discover the laureates of the 25th L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards {{!}} UNESCO |url=https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/discover-laureates-25th-loreal-unesco-women-science-international-awards |access-date=2023-06-14 |website=www.unesco.org |language=en}}</ref>

{{Quote|text=recognized for her important contributions in theoretical particle physics, in particular to the study of String Theory. Her research has furthered the theory's implications for the structure of matter and quantum gravity, which is also relevant to the description of black holes and the first instants after the big bang}}

In November 2023, Font was named to the [[BBC]]'s [[100 Women (BBC)|100 Women]] list as one of the world's inspiring and influential women.<ref name=BBC>{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2023 |title=BBC 100 Women 2023: Who is on the list this year? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/resources/idt-02d9060e-15dc-426c-bfe0-86a6437e5234 |access-date=2023-11-24 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

* {{cite journal |last1=Font |first1=A. |last2=Ibáñez |first2=L.E. |last3=Lüst |first3=D. |last4=Quevedo |first4=F. |title=Supersymmetry breaking from duality invariant gaugino condensation |journal=Physics Letters B |date=August 1990 |volume=245 |issue=3–4 |pages=401–408 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(90)90665-S |bibcode=1990PhLB..245..401F |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/207533 }}
